headline: High: Devin’s broad workspace/OAuth access combined with n8n’s server-side workflow execution creates dangerous default paths for data leakage, capability conflict, and cascading automation errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can read/write cloud workspace files and use MCP, while n8n can process server files and connected-system inputs. That creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path if Devin writes attacker-controlled content into a workflow input or shared file that n8n later treats as trusted. No explicit provenance controls are shown for either agent.
conditions: IF Devin writes untrusted text into a file or integration payload that n8n later parses as instructions
IF an n8n workflow reads shared files or connected-system messages without provenance checks
mitigations: Restrict n8n workflows to allowlisted input paths only.
Add a manual review step before n8n consumes Devin-authored artifacts.
Prefix all machine-generated content with non-executable markers.
Disable MCP routes that pass raw instructions between the agents.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and enforcement at workflow boundaries.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin is explicitly granted broad network egress, cloud workspace files, and write access to Slack/Linear/Jira/Notion, while n8n can read server files and send workflow data through many integrations. If both touch sensitive repo or ticket data, either agent can move it into external systems by default, making leakage and over-sharing plausible in normal operation.
conditions: IF Devin receives secrets, source code, or internal tickets and writes them to Slack/Notion/Jira
IF n8n workflows forward server files or workflow payloads to third-party integrations
mitigations: Remove write scopes from Devin unless needed for the task.
Limit n8n credentials to the minimum integration set.
Block sensitive folders from n8n file reads.
Use redaction before either agent posts to chat or ticketing systems.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention rules on both integration layers.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files and execute shell commands, and both have broad network egress. Devin also modifies git state, while n8n can run Execute Command on the server. If they target the same repo, workspace, or deployment surface, concurrent writes can overwrite each other or corrupt state without any locking mechanism being shown.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or server filesystem
IF n8n Execute Command and Devin shell actions run concurrently on shared mutable state
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent.
Serialize git writes through one orchestrator.
Disable n8n Execute Command for shared repos.
Use file locks around deployment artifacts.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is a long-running autonomous planner-executor, and n8n’s AI Agent node orchestrates tools as workflow nodes. That means Devin’s outputs can become n8n inputs, and n8n can then take actions through integrations or command nodes with little evidence of verification. The pair therefore supports default automation chains where one agent’s mistake propagates into real actions.
conditions: IF n8n consumes Devin-generated text, code, or plans as workflow input
IF the workflow triggers side effects such as tickets, messages, or command execution without human review
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any downstream action.
Require human approval for destructive workflow nodes.
Constrain Devin outputs to structured schemas.
Log and diff Devin outputs before n8n consumes them.
requires-engineering: add policy gates for action-taking nodes.

E_compliance.rationale: Devin is documented as touching source code, issue trackers, team chat, and docs, while n8n processes whatever the workflow handles and stores credentials on its server. The profiles do not prove a specific residency or certification mismatch, but they do show different retention and logging surfaces that can create compliance gaps when the same data class flows through both systems.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through both agents in the same workflow
IF one system retains logs or credentials longer than the other for the same data class
mitigations: Classify data before routing it through either agent.
Avoid sending regulated records into n8n workflows.
Shorten retention on logs and workflow history.
Review credential storage settings on n8n.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries for each integration.
